parser_limitations.limitation: Header declarations and inline signatures are sampled as C API facts; the extractor does not prove body-level behavior or all call-site contracts.
Behavior indicators are lexical or local-context signals and must be reviewed with surrounding C code before being treated as semantic contract drift.
A Rust binding reference establishes reachability evidence, not that the surrounding safe abstraction depends on the changed C contract.
Safe API exposure extraction is signature-oriented and can miss contracts expressed outside the function body or module-local helper path.
Error and nullability mappings are proximity facts; nearby C bindings are hints, not proof of an exact return-convention dependency.
Lifetime and ownership facts identify Rust-side patterns but do not prove that a specific C-side refcount or allocation rule changed.
Promoted warning evidence is sufficient for prioritization, but file-level or oracle-only context is reported as a limitation and not as a confirmed bug.

claim_policy: ranking and semantic claims are downgraded when strict gates fail

ablations.design_choice: Contract evidence from safety comments, error mappings, lifetime facts, and safe APIs raises stale-contract review targets above generic API drift.
Graph evidence keeps weak symbol-only matches below better-supported C/Rust contract evidence.
Impact gating helps keep C-only or weak-reachability drift below Rust-impact review targets.
